subject: Backdated SLA remediation request — Skyline AI production impact
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan@skyline.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors yesterday — request for remediation and accounting of SLA hits

Hi Soojin / Lauren,

Quick summary: yesterday between ~14:05–14:20 UTC we saw repeated 503s and very high tail latency (p95 -> p99.9 spike) for the batch inference route that serves our realtime product. This affected ~6% of our end-user requests for a ~15-minute window and caused a rollback on our side.

We captured logs/latency traces and attached a small excerpt (skyline-error-log-20250525.txt). We believe this qualifies as an SLA event per section 3.2 of our service agreement. We are looking for two things:

- A formal acknowledgement of the incident and root-cause summary (reasonable detail)
- A retroactive remediation offer (credit, free months, or other compensation) and commitment on preventive measures to avoid recurrence

Our renewal is active and we prefer to resolve this without a legal escalation. Can you confirm next steps and whether you can propose a remediation package by COB tomorrow (Jun 4)?

Thanks,
Evan Brooks
Head of Product, Skyline AI
E: evan@skyline.ai
T: +1 415-555-0198

Attachments (referenced): skyline-error-log-20250525.txt

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Evan Brooks <evan@skyline.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors yesterday — request for remediation and accounting of SLA hits

Hi Evan — thanks for the clear summary and the logs. I’m sorry Skyline ran into this.

We're opening a full post-mortem with engineering and ops; engineering is already pulling detailed traces and the service control plane metrics. I’ll own coordination and get you an initial acknowledgment and an ETA for the RCA by EOD tomorrow.

For the remediation package, we want to be constructive. Before I propose something public-facing, could you confirm two quick items:

1) The renewal term and committed monthly spend (I have DL-98431 in our system but want to ensure it's the right term).
2) Any downstream customer SLA guarantees you have that we should consider when sizing an offer (e.g., do you have pass-through SLAs where you must provide credits to your customers?).

If you’re ok, I’ll propose an initial remediation structure internally and come back with a specific offer.

— Soojin
So, Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Jun 2025 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Skyline AI incident — proposed remediation (internal)

Team,

Evan sent logs and is requesting a retroactive remediation offer. Quick context: 15-minute tail-latency outage, impacted ~6% of requests. Renewal DL-98431, ARR tier mid-enterprise (committed spend ~$60k/mo).

My proposal to close quickly and avoid escalation:
- Option A (preferred): 3 months of service credit applied to next billing cycle (equivalent to 25% of one month each, total credit = 75% of one month).
- Option B: Single lump-sum credit equal to 2 months of committed spend.
- Add-on: 90-day operational commitments — weekly syncs + two remediation engineering priorities (cache tuning + routing policy changes).

Rationale: keeps renewal intact, demonstrates good faith, limited financial exposure. I recommend Option A plus the operational commitments.

Please reply with approvals, adjustments, or if Finance/legal need to weigh in. I’ll package this into a short proposal (spreadsheet) and send to Evan.

Thanks,
So — Soojin

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Forwarding with my recommendation to approve Option A (3 x 25% monthly credit) + operational commitments.

Marissa notes: I want Finance to sign off on the accounting treatment (apply as a billing credit vs one-time rebate) and Legal to confirm there are no contract language traps for retroactive terms. If approved, I'll send the short proposal (attached) to Evan for sign-off.

Attachment: proposed-remedy-structure.xlsx

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, procurement@skyline.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Jun 2025 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Backdated SLA remediation request — Skyline AI production impact

Evan — thanks for your patience. We completed the internal review and engineering post-mortem. We acknowledge the service disruption and the impact on Skyline.

Approved remediation (final):
- Credit: three (3) monthly credits applied across the next billing cycle (each credit = 25% of your committed monthly spend under DL-98431; net effect = 75% of one month).
- Operational commitments: weekly 30-minute syncs for 90 days + two prioritized engineering tickets to harden the batch inference route (cache TTL tuning + routing fallbacks).
- Accounting: credit will be applied as billing credit and reflected on your next invoice; no changes to contract language.

Next steps:
1) Accept the remediation by replying to this thread with a line: "Skyline accepts the remediation offer as detailed."
2) We’ll send an approved concession term PDF and a DocuSign link to finalize the administrative acceptance.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/transaction/abc123-skyline-remedy
Attachment: approved-concession-term.pdf

Appreciate the partnership — we’ll follow up with an RCA in the next 48 hours and set the first weekly sync.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
SVP, Sales | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
